subject: Post-call recap: token window, streaming needs, and latency impact
messages:
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.com>
To: Robert Lowe <rlowe@acmehealth.com>, Aneeta Sharma <aneeta@finlytics.ai>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-09-15T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call recap: token window, streaming needs, and latency impact

Hi Robert / Aneeta —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our discovery so we have alignment before we draft a short technical proposal and MAP: 

- Primary goal: embed fast, interactive assistant into clinician workflow for chart summarization and question answering. Target: sub-350ms tail latency for 95th percentile on short queries (input ~200 tokens, output ~150 tokens) and acceptable 95th percentile up to 700ms for longer context summaries (input up to ~2,500 tokens, output 600+ tokens).
- Concurrency: initial pilot expects ~20 concurrent interactive users during peak; headroom target for Dedicated to 50 concurrent sessions.
- Throughput: batch workloads for nightly summarization (10k charts) — not latency sensitive, can use quantized variants to reduce cost.
- Streaming: clinicians want token-by-token streaming for quick partial reads on Q&A; confirm streaming is required for UI.
- Data retention / audit: logs need to be retained for 1 year; you mentioned SOC2 + HIPAA requirements.

Open questions we flagged:
1) Which flows need true streaming vs. chunked/resumable responses? (e.g., live Q&A vs. long report generation)
2) Expected peak tokens per minute and per hour for pilot (helps sizing capacity).
3) Any hard latency SLOs per route (we heard sub-350ms for simple Q&A; please confirm whether that is a strict SLO or a target).

Next steps we propose:
- We will draft a one-page perf/slo proposal that maps routes (quick-QA, long-summary, nightly-batch) to recommended model variants, q4 quantization, and concurrent slot counts.
- Internal follow-up with our infra eng (cc'd Neha) to confirm Dedicated pool sizing and streaming stack implications.
- Can we schedule a short technical sync next week (30 min) to agree token budgets and confirm streaming UX constraints?

Attachments: I will circulate a draft MAP + rough config after our internal sizing.

Thanks,
Stephanie Nguyen
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

From: Robert Lowe <rlowe@acmehealth.com>

Date: 2027-09-15T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: token window, streaming needs, and latency impact

Thanks Stephanie — good summary. A couple quick clarifications: 

- The 350ms figure is a firm UX requirement for the triage Q&A route (clinician types a one-sentence question, expects near-instant answer). Longer summary generation (the 2–3k token inputs) is allowed to be slower up to the 700–900ms range but we prefer under 800ms when possible.
- Streaming is required for the interactive Q&A flow — clinicians should see tokens as they arrive; partial answers are fine. For the long-summary flow, streaming is optional (we can accept a final payload for reports).
- Pilot peak: expect ~15–25 concurrent interactive clinicians during the first 6 weeks, with the possibility to double during scheduled training days. Peak tokens per minute: rough estimate 150k tokens/minute across all routes during training windows (we know this is a wide estimate).

I'll confirm the HIPAA/SOC2 audit evidence and share the contact from Security.

Can we do the tech sync on Tue 2027-09-21 10:00 AM PT?

—Robert
Director of Clinical AI
Acme Health
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
To: Robert Lowe <rlowe@acmehealth.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.com>, Aneeta Sharma <aneeta@finlytics.ai>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-09-16T08:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: token window, streaming needs, and latency impact

Thanks for confirming Robert — a few technical notes to make sizing concrete. I'm Rishi on the applied ML/inference team; looping in specifics so the MAP has numbers you can validate.

- Streaming implications: token-by-token streaming increases tail latency overhead slightly depending on network and client ACK behavior. For our optimized runtime on A100/DPUs we typically see a ~30–60ms extra per response overhead for streaming setups vs. non-streaming for small responses (<=200 output tokens). That overhead is amortized for long outputs.
- Per-token generation cost (median) on a 16-bit model: ~0.9ms/token on our baseline config. Quantized INT8 variants reduce per-token time to ~0.6–0.7ms/token but increase variance slightly; for 4k input+1k output, that maps to ~3–4s total compute if run single-threaded — but with batching and parallelism we can cut tail down.
- To hit 95p <350ms for the triage Q&A (avg 200 in + 150 out), we recommend: 3 concurrent inference slots backed by a low-latency variant (reduced context caching + prefix KV warmups), streaming enabled, and a dedicated pool size to support 25 concurrent users (assumes average 1.5 requests/sec per active clinician during bursts). This is a conservative plan that leaves headroom for spikes.
- For nightly summarization (10k charts), we recommend using our quantized batch pipeline with pre-tokenized chunks, no streaming, and retry/backoff for throughput. Cost/throughput tradeoffs in the attached spreadsheet.

I'll attach an initial sizing tab with: expected tokens/min, recommended GPU counts for Dedicated pilot, and a rough latency model. We'll refine after we get exact tokens/min data.

Rishi
Applied ML — Redwood Inference

Date: 2027-09-17T14:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: token window, streaming needs, and latency impact

Perfect — thanks Rishi and Robert. Action items and timeline: 

- Rishi: please finalize the sizing tab in acme-performance-configs.xlsx with 3 scenarios (conservative, expected, aggressive) and add estimated monthly committed GPU hours for each. Target by EOD 2027-09-18.
- Neha: can you validate that the 1-year log retention + SOC2/HIPAA packaging is available for RDW-2391 and prepare a short note for their security contact.
- Stephanie / Sales: I'll draft and send the one-page perf/SLO proposal + MAP (RDW-2391-mutual-action-plan.pdf) by 2027-09-18 morning and book the technical sync for Tue 2027-09-21 10:00 AM PT.

Robert — for the sync agenda:
1) Confirm strict SLOs per route (triage Q&A strict? long-summary target?)
2) Walk through Rishi's conservative/expected/aggressive sizing and tradeoffs (latency vs cost)
3) Streaming implementation details and client-side ACK behavior we may need to standardize
4) Next steps and procurement timing if we proceed with Dedicated pilot

Looking forward — I attached the draft MAP and the spreadsheet for your review. Please reply with any schedule conflicts.

Best,
Stephanie Nguyen
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference

Attachments: RDW-2391-mutual-action-plan.pdf, acme-performance-configs.xlsx
